# meta.lang — Page does not declare its language

- **Check ID:** `meta.lang`
- **Default severity:** `error`; users can override it in `seaworthy.config.json`.
- **Needs:** `html`
- **Standards:** WCAG 3.1.1
- **Source module:** `packages/verify/src/checks/meta.ts`
- **Prose page:** [`docs/checks/meta.lang.md`](../meta.lang.md) — embedded below verbatim; write it there, never here.

The `<html>` element has no `lang` attribute, or an invalid one.

## Why it matters

Screen readers pick their voice and pronunciation from the page language; browsers use it for hyphenation, quotes, and translation offers. A French page read in an English voice is unusable.

## What it checks

`<html lang="...">` must be present and look like a language code: two or three letters, optionally followed by subtags (`en`, `fa`, `pt-BR`, `zh-Hant`). Redirect stubs (`html.meta-refresh`) are skipped.

## How to fix

```html
<html lang="fa" dir="rtl">
```

Set it once in the base layout. For a right-to-left language also set `dir="rtl"`.

## Options

None.

## Standards

- [WCAG 3.1.1 Language of Page](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/language-of-page.html)
